To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel minimally invasive contrast agent injection technique can be applied both to animal studies and to clinical evaluations of inner-ear barrier function and fluid compartments with gadolinium (Gd)-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

the ultra-small-volume administration of contrast agent into the medial wall of middle ear cavity is a novel and minimally invasive technique that enables visualization of the dynamic distribution of the contrast agent in the inner ear compartments.

the minimally invasive administration technique of ultra-small-volume gadolinium-based contrast agent to the medial wall of rat middle ear cavity was effective for enhancing the inner ear and that the signal intensity of the inner ear compartments was significantly improved by using a fluid-attentuation inversion recovery sequence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel technique for the minimally invasive administration and visualization of contrast agents to the inner ear.
a new minimally invasive technique for the administration of a contrast agent to the inner ear and its application in the visualization of inner ear compartments.
a novel method to investigate inner ear barrier functions and to deliver drugs to the inner ear.

the use of a minimally invasive method for Gd-DOTA administration to the medial wall of middle ear cavity is feasible, and the dynamic distribution and enhancement effect of the inner ear can be visualized by MRI.
the present technique of Gd-DOT administration to the middle ear is a promising method to visualize and study the inner ear with MR imaging.
Gd-DOTA is a useful contrast agent for inner ear MRI, and the novel minimally invasive method is an efficient way for contrast agent delivery.

the inner ear can be visualized in vivo using a minimally invasive technique.
we have developed a novel technique that can be applied to animal studies and clinical evaluation of the inner ear.
we can use this method to study the inner ear in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inner ear can be imaged using MRI with a very small volume of contrast agent injected into the middle ear.
we can use a small volume of contrast agent (Gd-DOT) to enhance the signal in the inner ear, and this enhancement is dynamic.

it is possible to deliver a small amount of a contrast agent to the medial wall of a rat middle ear cavity and that the contrast agent is distributed in the cochlea, the vestibulum, and the ST in a dynamic fashion, with the vestibulum showing the highest uptake and the ST showing the lowest uptake.
